lead.name: Food Inflation Risk
lead.summary: The primary transmission channel for 2026. A below-normal monsoon with localised northern-belt deficits is enough to push pulses, oilseeds and select vegetables materially higher in H2 CY26 — even with adequate aggregate supply. Peak food inflation may land in Oct–Dec 2026, coinciding with the strongest El Niño phase and pre-Budget sensitivity.
drivers: Kharif pulses & oilseeds are price-sensitive to distribution, not just totals
2023 sugar episode (−8% output on uneven rain) as the recent template
Peak El Niño phase (Oct–Dec) aligns with the peak price-pressure window
RBI and the bond market are watching CPI-food as the binding constraint

channels.name: Drought Risk
channels.note: Buffered by 44.6% reservoir storage; northern belt most exposed late-season.

channels.name: Agriculture Risk
channels.note: Kharif (rice, soy, cotton, pulses) most exposed; southern output protected.

channels.name: Heatwave Risk
channels.note: El Niño years skew hot; pre- and post-monsoon windows the concern.

channels.name: Flood Risk
channels.note: El Niño suppresses the heaviest monsoon flooding vs La Niña years.

channels.name: Water / Hydro Risk
channels.note: Reservoir drawdown affects hydro generation (NHPC, JSW) into rabi season.

risk.riskInference: For India in 2026 the dominant channel is not drought — the reservoir buffer is adequate — but food inflation. The five supporting channels all feed into or sit alongside that primary read. The analytically important point is the timing alignment: the peak El Niño phase (Oct–Dec), peak food-price pressure, and pre-Budget political sensitivity all land in the same window, which is what makes the food-inflation channel the one to position around rather than the headline monsoon number.
